title: Counting-sort prefix phase
statement: Let a counting-sort input have $n$ items with keys in $\{0,\ldots,N-1\}$, and assume the address bounds, key-cell bounds, and required disjointness conditions for the source, destination, and counter ranges. If the counters initially contain the frequencies of keys among the first $n$ items (with counter zero equal to $0$), then the prefix-sum program has an execution of cost at most $25N+6$ that ends with loop index $N$, counters containing the cumulative frequencies through each key, and memory agreeing with its initial value outside the destination and counter ranges.
hypotheses_covered: Counting-sort preconditions: word bound, source/destination/counter bounds, item and key contents, key range, and required interval disjointness
Initial state has loop index $n$, counters containing the counted key frequencies, and agrees with initial memory outside destination and counter ranges
caveat: The bundled counted-state and summed-state predicates are not informally defined in the supplied descriptions.
